Job description
DLA Piper is, at its core, bold, exceptional, collaborative and supportive. Our people are the backbone, heart and soul of our firm. Wherever you are in your professional journey, DLA Piper is a place you can engage in meaningful work and grow your career. Let’s see what we can achieve. Together. Summary DLA Piper is seeking a talented writer as a Senior Attorney to join its Litigation group, Product Liability, Mass Torts & Class Actions subgroup, to work with its Class Actions group. This position is a non-partnership track and is open to any US office, with a preference for New York metropolitan based candidates. Responsibilities Drafting briefs, motions and memoranda Reviewing and drafting discovery responses Analysis of discovery to inform case strategy and motion drafting Prepare deposition outlines Minimum Education JD Experience Minimum of 6 years of experience Experience drafting litigation documents, such as motions to dismiss, written discovery and summary judgment motions Bar Admission Admission in the bar for the jurisdiction in which you are applying Essential Job Expectations While the specific job requirements of a DLA Piper position may vary depending upon scope of the job and area of specialty, there are certain universal requirements that are expected of all DLA Piper employees, which include but are not limited to: Effectively communicate, verbally and in writing, with clients, lawyers, business professionals, and third parties; Produce deliverables, answer phone calls, and reply to correspondence in an efficient and responsive manner; Provide timely, accurate, and quality work product; Successfully meet deadlines, expectations, and perform work duties as required; Foster positive work relationships; Comply with all firm policies and practices; Engage in both physical and sedentary activity, such as (a) working at a computer for extended periods of time, including on-screen reading and typing; (b) participating in digital/virtual conference calls; (c) participating in meetings as needed; Ability to work under pressure and manage competing demands in a fast-paced environment; Perform all other duties, tasks or projects as assigned. Our employees are expected to embrace and uphold our firm values as a part of our DLA Piper culture. We are committed to excellence in how we represent our clients and develop our people. Physical Demands Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally and all other sedentary criteria are met. Work Environment-The firm’s work location requirements may be modified at the firm’s discretion Hybrid - Regular in-office presence with some flexibility for work-from-home Disclaimer The purpose of this job description is to provide a concise statement of the work elements and to organize and present the information in a standardized way. It is not intended to describe all the elements of the work that may be performed by every individual in this classification, nor should it serve as the sole criteria for personnel decisions and actions. The job duties, requirements, and expectations for this position may be modified at the Firm’s discretion at any time. This job description does not change the at-will nature of employment. Application Process All candidates must provide a cover letter, resume, transcript, and a writing sample not substantially edited by anyone other than the applicant. Please apply online if you are a direct applicant. Applicants must apply directly online instead of sending application materials via email. If you have a request for an accommodation during the application process or if you have any questions about the process, please contact LitigationTalent@talent.us.dlapiper.com. Please add dlapi

Job description
Troutman Pepper Locke is seeking an Associate to join our Finance & Banking Practice Group, specifically within the Corporate Trust Subgroup. This position offers the opportunity to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, with the flexibility to be based in any state where Troutman Pepper Locke has an office. The ideal candidate will have one to five years of structured finance experience, particularly in representing trustees and/or collateral agents. We welcome candidates from a variety of backgrounds, and for those with one or two years of legal experience, while an interest in finance or accounting is advantageous, we value hard work and a history of demonstrated success above all else. We are committed to supporting the growth and development of associates at every level. The role involves representing trustees and/or collateral agents in structured finance transactions, providing legal advice and support on a variety of structured finance matters, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating transaction documents, and collaborating with other attorneys and staff to ensure the delivery of high-quality legal services. You can learn more about our Corporate Trust practice on our website. Candidates must demonstrate a strong work ethic, maturity, and effective communication skills. All candidates must be licensed and in good standing in the state in which they practice. The salary range for this position is $225,000 - $310,000, dependent on years of experience. For inquiries or additional information on this position, please contact Linda Bystrowski.

Job description
Wilson Sonsini’s energy practice is recruiting 3rd to 7th year associates with a transactional focus in the energy sector. The ideal candidate will be comfortable analyzing and drafting key project development contracts such as power purchase agreements and other offtake arrangements, working on framework commercial agreements and joint venture transactions, and serving as the go-to associate on project and portfolio acquisitions and related financing support. An ability to use and adapt a range of commercial structures for solar, wind, geothermal, natural gas, battery, nuclear projects, and data center and utility buyers will be valuable; a desire to develop mastery of structuring and negotiating energy project development transactions will be essential. This position will involve daily direct contact with a wide range of clients, Wilson Sonsini partners, and counterparty counsel, so strong communication and project management skills are required. Our ECS team is located in our Boston, DC, Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, and Seattle offices and would welcome attorneys who want to join the team in those locations and advance our mission. We may consider other office locations. Wilson Sonsini fields an integrated team of lawyers providing high-value services to innovative, cutting-edge clients in the energy sector. Our work includes project development and commercial transactions, project finance and securitization, corporate finance, and energy regulatory. Our clients range from game-changing nuclear and enhanced geothermal companies proving their technologies, through leading independent power producers acquiring and building gigawatts of new PV and battery projects, to global hyper-scalers pursuing unprecedented regulatory models in support of energy supply for AI. Like our clients, we move fast and work hard; like our clients, we are not afraid to take on the creative challenge of doing something new and difficult. Who We Are ArentFox Schiff is an award-winning, globally recognized law firm that delivers sophisticated, innovative, and practical legal solutions to clients around the world. Job Description and Salary ArentFox Schiff LLP is seeking a patent agent or patent attorney with a minimum of five years of experience preparing and prosecuting patent applications in the biotechnology field at a law firm. The ideal candidate will have substantial experience drafting patent applications directed to in vitro diagnostic assays, along with familiarity in one or more of the following areas: immunoassays, CRISPR-based assays, nucleic acid sequencing and quantification, and related probes, kits, and reagents. Experience with computational biology is a plus but is not required. This position will be based in the firm’s San Francisco or New York office. Ideal candidates will hold an M.S. or Ph.D. in molecular biology or a closely related discipline. Candidates who do not hold a graduate degree, but who possess a B.S. in a relevant field combined with five or more years of post-graduate laboratory or industry experience will also be considered. For the patent agent role, active registration with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (i.e., admission to the Patent Bar) is required. For the patent attorney role, active bar admission in California or New York (depending on which office the candidate will be in) is required in addition to Patent Bar registration. All candidates must demonstrate familiarity with patent databases and search tools, experience managing patent portfolios, and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. ArentFox Schiff LLP offers a competitive salary and excellent benefits. Interested candidates should submit a resume, law school transcript, and a writing sample. The good faith base salary range for this position is a minimum of $200,000 to a maximum of $300,000 per year. The actual salary rate offered to candidates within that range will depend on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, years of relevant experience, position type, education, applicable bar admissions, and the candidate’s overall qualifications for the position as assessed by the Firm. In addition to a competitive base salary, we offer a comprehensive bonus program with opportunities for discretionary incentives that may include productivity, business development, and merit-based components, subject to applicable policies. That’s why we offer a wide array of flexible benefit options designed to help you live healthy, live well, and live for tomorrow. In addition to medical, dental, vision, profit-sharing, generous paid time off, and numerous other benefits, we also provide a flexible reimbursement account that helps pay for the things that contribute to your personal well-being, in your own way. Foley Hoag LLP is seeking talented attorneys who have recently completed or are currently completing a judicial clerkship to join our firm. We welcome applications from former or current clerks looking to leverage their experience in a dynamic and collaborative law firm environment. Who Should Apply We encourage applications from individuals who have: • Recently completed or are currently completing a judicial clerkship in a federal or state court. • Strong academic credentials from an accredited law school. • Exceptional legal research, writing, and analytical skills. • The ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. About Foley Hoag Founded in 1943, Foley Hoag has grown into an award-winning, international law firm that focuses on innovative industries and high-stakes litigation. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, and a connected, challenging, professional, and fun place for you to thrive in the next chapter of your career. At Foley Hoag, we welcome, develop, and celebrate talented and diverse individuals in an innovative, mutually respectful, and intellectually rigorous community, and bring unique perspectives to collaborative teams that deliver exceptional advice and craft bespoke legal solutions for our clients and our world. Foley Hoag LLP is an equal opportunity employer. This means that Foley Hoag LLP considers applicants for employment, and makes employment decisions without unlawful regard to sex, race, color, religion, citizenship, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or domestic partner/civil union status, military service, veteran status, disability status, and any other characteristic covered by applicable federal, state or local nondiscrimination laws. Associate - Tax - Energy & Infrastructure Job Locations | US-NY-New York | US-TX-Houston | US-DC-Washington, D.C. | US-CA-Los Angeles | US-IL-Chicago | US-TX-Austin Minimum Experience Minimum of 5 years Department Tax Practice Group Transactional Tax About Latham & Watkins Latham & Watkins is one of the world’s leading global law firms advising the businesses and institutions that drive the global economy. We are the market leaders in major financial and business centers globally and offer unmatched expertise and resources to help you grow from an intellectually curious self-starter into an exceptional lawyer. If you aspire to be the best, this is where you belong. About the Practice Group Latham tax lawyers create innovative structures and solve complex tax issues for a full spectrum of clients. Our tax lawyers advise multinational corporations, financial institutions, private equity funds, domestic corporations, joint ventures, emerging companies, special purpose acquisition companies (SPACs), and tax-exempt organizations. The firm has a long and rich history with the US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and US Department of the Treasury, dating back to founding partner Dana Latham’s tenure as Commissioner of the IRS under President Eisenhower. Today, more than 100 tax lawyers around the globe collaborate across offices and disciplines to address tax issues that arise in the context of transactions, controversies, and general business operations. While tax questions are often complex, we develop practical, commercial answers for clients across a range of industries. About the Role The Energy & Infrastructure group is seeking an associate with a minimum of 5 years of experience to join our team. Candidate should have experience with financings and M&A pertaining to power and energy transition transactions with some substantive experience with energy tax credit transactions. Ideal candidate will have experience that includes documenting and negotiating complex joint ventures, tax equity transactions, tax credit transfers, familiarity with partnership tax rules, and experience drafting and negotiating tax provisions in partnership agreements, credit agreements, and purchase and sale documentation. M&A Clearance Team Associate Attorney
Kirkland & Ellis · CHICAGO, DC · Antitrust, M&A HSR Counseling FTC DOJ 2026-06-25
Job description
We are currently seeking junior attorneys with outstanding credentials and qualifications to join our Mergers & Acquisitions Clearance Team in Chicago or Washington, DC. Ideal candidates will have 1 year of Antitrust/Competition related M&A clearance experience. A background in regulatory/corporate M&A or experience working for private equity fund clients is a plus. The Mergers & Acquisitions Clearance Team handles compliance with the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act (the “HSR Act”) and coordinates with our European-based team on international merger control compliance. The Team supports busy and growing antitrust, corporate and private equity practices. This position is focused on regulatory antitrust matters, rather than antitrust litigation. The ideal candidate will be expected to assess HSR reportability, prepare HSR forms, and manage filing preparation, including coordination with the client, the corporate team and opposing counsel. Current Team members and other antitrust partners will provide additional training and support on these job requirements. The candidate may be asked to work on substantive antitrust analysis of competitor transactions, Second Request responses and general antitrust counseling matters. Qualified candidates must have excellent drafting and communication skills, exceptional attention to detail and the ability to work effectively within deadlines. Kirkland & Ellis LLP offers a competitive salary structure as well as a robust offering of benefits to all of its employees and attorneys. Compensation is based upon the roles and responsibilities of the position, the experience and education of the applicant and/or employee and is aligned with internal pay equity within Kirkland & Ellis LLP itself. The hiring salary range for this position is between $225,000 and $235,000. These figures are not representative of the full compensation range for this position.

Job Description Opportunity We are seeking an associate with experience in defined benefit pension plans and related liabilities to join our growing Labor Transactions Practice. The associate will work closely with senior lawyers on corporate, finance, and restructuring matters, advising clients on complex pension issues arising in transactions, financings, and restructurings, particularly where pension liabilities are a material component of deal economics. The role includes advising on multiemployer and single-employer defined benefit pension plans and analyzing pension liabilities, including exposure arising from participation in and withdrawal from multiemployer plans and plan terminations (including PBGC-related matters). The associate will also support transactional teams in evaluating pension liabilities in diligence and deal structuring and developing strategies to allocate, mitigate, or eliminate such liabilities in acquisitions, financings, and restructurings, while addressing withdrawal liability disputes and advising on compliance with ERISA, PBGC requirements, and related regulatory frameworks. About the Practice Akin’s Labor Transactions Practice advises clients on the labor and employment aspects of complex corporate transactions, including mergers and acquisitions, private equity, credit, hybrid and other capital solutions investments, restructurings, and other strategic transactions. We work with public and private companies, private equity sponsors, and other investors to identify, assess, and manage labor‑related risks in connection with deal activity. Our work includes diligence and structuring advice relating to sophisticated labor strategy in transactional contexts, including in connection with unionized and non‑union workforces, collective bargaining agreements, executive compensation matters, worker classification, and WARN Act compliance. We regularly partner with Akin’s corporate, private equity, capital markets, restructuring, and employee benefits teams to deliver integrated, practical solutions for clients navigating complex transactions. Job description
Municipal Associate The Seattle office of Ogden Murphy Wallace, P.L.L.C. is seeking an associate attorney to join its municipal practice. Applicants must have a strong background in municipal law, developed research and writing skills, litigation experience, superior academic credentials, and the ability to work closely with multiple attorneys and staff. The preferred candidate will have at least three years of legal experience with, or a demonstrated interested in, the substantive law surrounding land use/zoning matters; public records and open government requirements; public bidding and contracting; municipal ethics; tribal law; water law; or personnel, employment, and labor issues. The position involves the following responsibilities: Support and advise City Councils, Mayors, City staff members and local boards/commissions; Research and analyze complex issues; Draft and review ordinances, resolutions, policies and procedures; Provide telephonic and email advice to clients as needed; Counsel clients to ensure compliance with state, federal, and local laws; Attend meetings of City Councils, boards, and commissions; Communicate with prospective and existing clients in a professional and courteous manner; Represent municipal clients in judicial litigation and in administrative appeals, hearings, and other proceedings; Provide legal review of municipal documents under the Public Records Act; and Negotiate/draft/review contracts, deeds, leases, bid documents and bonds, easements, interlocal agreements, and other documents. Desired Skills: Excellent research, writing, and analytical skills; Team-oriented yet self-motivated mentality; Attention to detail; Display of ownership with job responsibilities; and The ability to learn quickly. Ogden Murphy Wallace is a multi-specialty firm primarily serving Pacific Northwest clients for over 100 years. OMW takes pride in providing exceptional legal services while, at the same time, offering its employees a professional, friendly, and inclusive community, as well as a fun work environment. OMW offers a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k) and profit-sharing plan, paid time off, ten paid holidays per year, paid family leave, life insurance, and long-term disability coverage. The base compensation range for this position is $145,000 to $175,000 a year. Other compensation includes an annual discretionary profit-sharing contribution, non-discretionary bonus opportunities and additional discretionary bonus consideration. We encourage professional development by providing programs, training, and opportunities to do interesting work. Ogden Murphy Wallace is committed to providing an inclusive and welcoming environment for all members of our staff, vendors and clients. OMW is an Equal Opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, age, national origin, genetic information, veteran status, disability status or any other category prohibited by local, state or federal law. This policy applies to all aspects of employment, including recruitment, placement, promotion, transfer, demotion, compensation, benefits, social and recreational activities, termination, and all other terms and conditions of employment. To be considered for this exciting opportunity, interested and qualified candidates should submit a cover letter and resume to Shari Tipp, Human Resources Director, at stipp@omwlaw.com or 701 Fifth Avenue, Suite 5600, Seattle, WA 98104. We look forward to hearing from you!
